name: SRE · VM guest OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m
titleTemplate: SRE · VM guest OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m · ${cluster_name} · ${node} · ${name}
description: Checks VM guest OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.
remediation:
1. Locate the cluster and resource named in the alert. Compare the reported metric with the guest OS or Kubernetes API.
2. Review the same time window for workload changes, limits, restarts and storage or memory pressure.
3. Apply a workload-specific correction and verify recovery; do not delete data or raise limits automatically.

name: SRE · VM CPU scheduler wait above 10 percent · 10m
titleTemplate: SRE · VM CPU scheduler wait above 10 percent · 10m · ${cluster_name} · ${namespace} · ${name}
description: Each virtual CPU spends more than 10% of wall time, on average, waiting to run on a host CPU throughout observed samples in 10 minutes. KubeVirt scheduler delay is not automatically the VMware CPU Ready counter. Health is attached to the Harvester host; the title identifies the VM.
remediation: Check the named VM and its Harvester host. Compare host CPU busy, VM CPU consumption, allocation and competing VMs. Review scheduling and overcommit. Adjust the baseline to the workload before paging.

name: SRE · VM disk response above 20ms · 10m
query: min_over_time((((max by(k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name,drive) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_storage_read_times_seconds_total{drive!~".*(cloudinit|cdrom).*"}[5m]))+max by(k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name,drive) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_storage_write_times_seconds_total{drive!~".*(cloudinit|cdrom).*"}[5m])))/((max by(k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name,drive) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_storage_iops_read_total{drive!~".*(cloudinit|cdrom).*"}[5m]))+max by(k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name,drive) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_storage_iops_write_total{drive!~".*(cloudinit|cdrom).*"}[5m]))) >= 1))*1000 * on(k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) group_left(cluster_name,node) (label_replace(max by(k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name,node) (kubevirt_vmi_info{phase="running"}), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)")))[10m:30s])
description: Combined virtual disk read/write response exceeds 20 ms over observed 10-minute samples with at least 1 operation/s. Idle and cloud-init disks are excluded. This initial threshold needs a workload baseline. Health is attached to the host; the title identifies VM and drive.
remediation: Compare VM read/write times and IOPS with host disk response, queues and Longhorn volume/replica health. Check guest load and snapshots at the same time. This does not identify the faulty physical disk by itself.

name: SRE · VM filesystem above 90 percent used · 15m
titleTemplate: SRE · VM filesystem above 90 percent used · ${cluster_name} · ${namespace} · ${name} · ${disk_name}
description: A filesystem reported by the VM guest agent remains above 90% used throughout observed samples over 15 minutes. Excludes temporary, boot, runtime and loop filesystems. Missing guest data does not imply free space. Health attaches to the host; the title identifies the VM and disk. Bind mounts of the same guest device are counted once.
remediation: Check free space inside the named VM filesystem, growth, logs and retention. Compare guest filesystem capacity with its virtual disk and Longhorn volume. Expand only through the supported storage and guest-filesystem process. Do not delete files automatically.

name: SRE · Virtualization metrics scrape failing · 3m
description: An observed KubeVirt or Longhorn target has no successful scrape in the last three minutes. Check target discovery separately when a target disappears.
remediation: Check collector logs, current KubeVirt CA, target TLS names, API discovery RBAC and internal endpoint access. Refresh the copied public CA after rotation and upgrade the module. Never disable certificate validation.
